title: Integral quasi-section through a closed fibre point meeting a nearby open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $S$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $x\in X$, set $s=f(x)$, and suppose $x$ is closed in the fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], meaning that its singleton is closed in that fibre. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose that there is $x^{\prime}\in V$ such that $x\in\overline{\{x^{\prime}\}}$ and $f(x^{\prime})\ne s$. Then there are an integral closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] and its generic point $z$ [def-sc-generic-point] such that $x\in i(Z)$, $i(z)\in V$, $f(i(z))\ne s$, and $f\circ i$ is quasi-finite at the point of $Z$ above $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Here $\overline{\{i(z)\}}=i(Z)$ as subsets of $X$, so $i(z)$ specializes to $x$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, more-morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, statement and proof, especially the explicit choice Z = closure of {z} with its induced reduced scheme structure. The integrality and generic-point formulation record this choice, rather than an arbitrary Z in the displayed statement.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], $X$ is locally Noetherian. Put $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$. Choose a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $x$ from the covering in [pqf-def-locnoeth], and write $\mathfrak p\subset R$ for $x$. The canonical-local-spectrum statement [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] identifies $B=R_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. It is nonzero, since $\mathfrak p$ is proper. Write $c:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ for the canonical morphism; it maps $\mathfrak m_B$ to $x$ and its image consists of the generalizations of $x$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, local-spectrum reduction; Tag 05GT, preceding lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open, Noetherianness; Tags 01T6 and 00FN.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the local homomorphism induced by $f$. The morphism $f\circ c$ equals $\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\varphi}\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], both correspond to $(s,\varphi)$. By the canonical-local-spectrum description and the prime-localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], the only prime of $A$ mapping to $s$ is $\mathfrak m_A$. Consequently the primes of $B$ mapping to $s$ are exactly $V(\mathfrak m_AB)$: contraction contains $\mathfrak m_A$ if and only if it equals this maximal ideal. Hence $W=c^{-1}(V)\setminus V(\mathfrak m_AB)$ is open and lies in the punctured spectrum $P=\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus\{\mathfrak m_B\}$. It is nonempty: $x^{\prime}$ is a generalization of $x$, hence lifts under $c$, and any such lift lies in $W$ because $x^{\prime}\in V$ and $f(x^{\prime})\ne s$.

source.place: Tags 01J6 and 01J7 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring and lemma-specialize-points); the canonical local-spectrum commutative square preceding lemma-specialize-points. Tag 05GT, open avoiding the closed base point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-punctured-local-closed-points] to the nonzero Noetherian local ring $B$ and the nonempty open (hence locally closed) $W\subseteq P$. Obtain $\mathfrak q\in W$ closed in $P$. Since $B$ is local, $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak m_B$ and $\mathfrak m_B\in V(\mathfrak q)$. Closedness of $\{\mathfrak q\}$ in $P$ says $V(\mathfrak q)\cap P=\{\mathfrak q\}$. Thus the only primes of $B$ containing $\mathfrak q$ are $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak m_B$. Set $u=c(\mathfrak q)$. Then $u\in V$, $f(u)\ne s$ and $u$ specializes to $x$.

source.place: Tag 05GT, lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open, choice of a closed point in the punctured spectrum by Properties Tag 02IM.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] on $T=\overline{\{u\}}\subseteq X$ to obtain its reduced induced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. Its image is $T$, so it contains $x$. The subset $T$ is nonempty and irreducible: every open of $T$ containing any specialization of $u$ contains $u$, so any two nonempty opens of $T$ intersect at $u$. Thus $Z$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The point $z$ above $u$ is generic in $Z$, since the closed-immersion homeomorphism identifies its closure with $T$. In particular $i(z)=u\in V$ and $f(i(z))\ne s$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, construction of the reduced closure; Schemes Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme; Properties Tag 01ON, lemma-characterize-integral.

proof.text: Let $a\in Z$ lie above $x$, and let $b\in Z$ be a generalization of $a$. Using the Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ from step 1, write $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$ for $u$; then $\mathfrak rB=\mathfrak q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization]. Every generalization $i(b)$ of $x$ lies in this chart and corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak l\subseteq\mathfrak p$: the first inclusion expresses membership in $T=\overline{\{u\}}$ and the second expresses specialization to $x$. Its extension $\mathfrak lB$ contains $\mathfrak q$, so step 3 gives $\mathfrak lB=\mathfrak q$ or $\mathfrak m_B$. Contraction gives $i(b)=u$ or $x$, hence $b=z$ or $a$. The point $a$ is closed in $Z_s$: by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the closed-immersion embedding [def-weil-closed-immersion], this fibre is a subspace of $X_s$, where $x$ is closed by hypothesis. If $b$ belongs to $Z_s$ and specializes to $a$ in $Z_s$, it also specializes in $Z$; the alternative $b=z$ is excluded by $f(u)\ne s$. Thus $a$ has no other generalization in $Z_s$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, reduced-closure construction; Tag 05GT, the two points of Spec(B/q); Algebra Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization. This spells out the topological closed-fibre criterion instead of invoking local-ring quasi-finiteness implicitly.

proof.text: The composite $g=f\circ i$ is locally of finite type: for every affine $\operatorname{Spec}R_0\subseteq S$ and affine $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R_0)$, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] gives finitely many $R_0$-algebra generators of $C$. The inverse image under $i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the images of these generators generate $C/I$. These inverse images cover $Z$, giving the required affine finite-type charts. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-fibre-point-quasifinite-criterion] to $g$, $a$ and the two fibre properties proved in step 5. It is quasi-finite at $a$. Together with step 4 this gives every conclusion, including $\overline{\{i(z)\}}=i(Z)$.

source.place: Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, (3) implies (1); Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize; Tag 05GU, final quasi-finiteness conclusion.
